# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a working notebook rather than a textbook. The chapters are posts I wrote while reading, teaching, and consulting on applied econometrics, often because a colleague or a student asked a question that did not have a tidy answer in the books I had. Each one stands on its own. The order did not follow a plan, and the same topic sometimes appears more than once as my understanding changed.

The common question is the one Angrist and Pischke emphasize: what is being identified, by what variation, under what assumptions. The posts ask that question in different settings: interactions and marginal effects, fixed and correlated random effects, matching and weights, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, count models, TMLE and AIPW, mediation, proximal causal inference, partial interference, conjoint and list experiments, uplift modeling, and policy trees.

Most examples are in R. I use Stata where it is more natural, and sometimes Python or Julia when the package is better there. The two companion books, [Introduction to Causal Econometrics](https://xiangao.github.io/causal_econometrics_guide/) and [Causal Econometrics with Julia](https://xiangao.github.io/causal_econometrics_julia/), organize the same material more systematically. This collection is the messier version: useful when I want to see how a specific method behaves on a specific problem.

## Where to start {.unnumbered}

Forty-eight chapters in no particular order is not a reading order. Three routes through the
material, for readers who want one:

**Foundations.** What a coefficient means before any causal language is attached.
[Interpreting interaction in a regression model](interaction-regression.qmd) →
[Marginal effects in models with fixed effects](marginal-effects-fe.qmd) →
[Fixed or random effect, or both?](fixed-random-effect.qmd) →
[Matching and weighting, part 1](matching-part1.qmd) →
[part 2](weighting-part2.qmd).

**Modern causal estimation.** Nuisance functions estimated by machine learning, with the
estimand held fixed.
[Machine learning for causal effects](tmle.qmd) →
[Recent causal inference tools](npcausal-tools.qmd), which covers AIPW and double machine
learning →
[Longitudinal modified treatment policies](lmtp.qmd) →
[Intro to proximal causal inference](proximal-intro.qmd) →
[the proximal simulation](proximal-simulation.qmd).

**Panel and policy methods.** Designs where the variation comes from timing.
[Extended TWFE and other DiD estimators](extended-twfe.qmd) →
[Causal panel, and why DDDiD](causal-panel.qmd) →
[Synthetic control](synthetic-control.qmd) →
[Causal forest in panel data](causal-forest-panel.qmd) →
[Policy learning by policytree](policytree.qmd).

Chapters outside these routes are self-contained and can be read on their own.

## How to cite {.unnumbered}

Ao, Xiang. *Topics on Econometrics and Causal Inference*. <https://xiangao.github.io/blog_book/>.

```bibtex
@book{ao_topics_econometrics,
  author = {Ao, Xiang},
  title  = {Topics on Econometrics and Causal Inference},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://xiangao.github.io/blog_book/}
}
```
